evidence.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD by following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
Manasseh also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem I will put My Name.”
In both courtyards of the house of the LORD, he built altars to all the host of heaven.
He sacrificed his own son in the fire, practiced sorcery and divination, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

Manasseh even took the carved Asherah pole he had made and set it up in the temple, of which the LORD had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish My Name forever.
But the people did not listen and Manasseh led them astray, so that they did greater evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.

this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I am bringing such calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah that the news will reverberate in the ears of all who hear it.

He abandoned the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.

c: Josiah, who reigned in Judah from 640 to 609
, was a godly man, unlike his grandfather Manasseh and his father, Amon. Josiah “turned to the
with all his heart and soul and strength, obeying all the laws of Moses” (
The kingdom of Judah was grossly idolatrous and wicked during Manasseh’s reign (697–642
). Despite Manasseh’s own repentance toward the end of his reign, conditions continued to worsen under his son Amon (642–640
), who was so bad that his own officials assassinated him, and the eight-year-old Josiah was placed on the throne (
When Josiah was sixteen, he began “to seek the God of his ancestor David” (

). From that point on, he was dedicated to purifying the worship of the people of God. At twenty, Josiah began eradicating pagan places of worship, especially the despised pagan worship center at Bethel. Josiah fulfilled prophecy (
) by destroying its altar and burning the bones of pagan priests to desecrate the site (
When Josiah was twenty-six, he organized repairs to the Temple (
). In the process, the priest Hilkiah found the Book of the Law and read it to Josiah, who was devastated by its pronouncements against apostasy (

). He then sought more fully to obey God’s instructions and to lead the people in worshiping the Lord. He celebrated Passover as the law demanded, destroyed many artifacts used in Baal and sun worship, and eliminated pagan shrines in Judah (
). In all this, Josiah was apparently supported by the prophets Zephaniah and Jeremiah, who spoke for God during his time.
Josiah was not sensitive to God’s voice on one significant occasion, however, and it cost him his life (

, Pharaoh Neco marched toward Carchemish to reinforce the Assyrian army against Babylon. Josiah delayed Neco at Megiddo, perhaps wanting to support the Babylonians. Neco insisted that the Lord wanted him to fight Babylon, but Josiah attacked him and was killed in battle. Josiah was greatly mourned by Jeremiah and the people of Judah (

Though Josiah was faithful, the people were not; once he died, his sons and successors began to turn away from the Lord. In spite of Jeremiah’s increased efforts, the people did not repent. The turbulent years that followed Josiah’s death soon ended with the destruction of Jerusalem and the exile of its citizens to Babylon (605–586
) certainly cannot be attributed to his faithfulness to the Lord but to the Lord’s continued honoring of his covenant promises (see also

) conducted a number of military campaigns, none was directed against Judah until later in Manasseh’s reign, probably around 650–648
). Ashurbanipal’s attention was on building projects, religious pursuits, and the arts, including a great library. •
